reason: Claude Code's own command-safety check, not the bench sandbox or the bench hook, refused one Bash call, and the reviewer then ended without writing artifacts/composition.json. The refused call is the skill's step that accounts the verifier's return: it ran account_verifier_return.py, then echo "exit=$?", then a python3 -c one-liner that prints json.dumps(d, indent=1)[:1500]. The client runs under --permission-mode dontAsk, where a command the check would ask about is refused instead ("Permission to use Bash has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode"). Every earlier Bash call of the attempt ran. Three replays with the frozen client 2.1.294, the attempt's isolation-settings.json with its paths moved to a scratch folder, the flags of dispatch.sh and claude-haiku-5-5 reproduce it: every call that combined echo "exit=$?" with a Python slice [:1500] was refused (4 calls, 3 distinct commands, all refused), and every call with only one of the two ran (10 calls, all ran; 6 more calls with neither also ran). The rule applies to any Claude model: the four review-code reviews of 2026-10-12-last-push-claude-review-code-sonnet kept as reviewer-stop hit the same refusal through other command shapes (a heredoc, sed -i, cd ... &&). The stop comes from the harness's permission mode, not from the setup or the task. It is not replaced: on 2026-10-28 the owner chose to fix the harness first and freeze review-code again, so this run is superseded (superseded.v1.json) and no queue runs it.
usage_note: Priced from the attempt's 29 requests at the Haiku rate for prompts up to 100,000 tokens; the client reported $0.11. It stays in the run's spend.
